lean.statement:
{J : ℕ} (hJ : 2 ≤ J) {h : ℝ} (hh : 0 < h) :
    let t := fun i : Fin J => h/2*(1-Real.cos ((i : ℝ)/(J-1 : ℝ)*Real.pi))
    let ell := fun j : Fin J => Lagrange.basis Finset.univ t j
    let Lambda := sSup ((fun s : ℝ => ∑ j : Fin J, |(ell j).eval s|) '' Icc 0 h)
    let omega := fun i j : Fin J => ∫ s in 0..t i, (t i-s)*(ell j).eval s
    let momentumWeight := fun j : Fin J => ∫ s in 0..h, (ell j).eval s
    (∀ i, t i ∈ Icc 0 h) ∧ Function.Injective t ∧
    t ⟨J-1,by omega⟩ = h ∧
    (∀ i j, (ell i).eval (t j) = if i=j then 1 else 0) ∧
    (∀ s : ℝ, ∑ j : Fin J, (ell j).eval s = 1) ∧
    1 ≤ Lambda ∧
    (∀ i, (∑ j : Fin J, |omega i j|) ≤ (t i)^2/2*Lambda ∧
      (∑ j : Fin J, |omega i j|) ≤ h^2/2*Lambda) ∧
    (∑ j : Fin J, momentumWeight j) = h
approved_definition_context: Fin J is the finite index0,...,J-1; J-1 inside a real annotation is real subtraction after coercion. Lagrange.basis(univ,t,j) is the real polynomial product over k!=j of C((t_j-t_k)^(-1))*(X-C(t_k)); ell.eval s is real polynomial evaluation. For distinct nodes this is exactly product(s-t_k)/(t_j-t_k).

sSup is the conditionally complete real supremum. Set.image(F,Icc0h) is the range of F on the closed real interval. Interval integrals are Lebesgue integrals with orientation a..b; all displayed intervals here have nonnegative endpoints in order. Real.cos and Real.pi have their usual meanings.
